subject: Ghanaian Language
name: Basic 5 Ghanaian Language
description: Part 2 of the Basic 5 Ghanaian Language curriculum focuses on developing writing skills, including penmanship, composition, and grammar usage. It also includes extensive reading to foster a culture of reading.

subStrands.title: Penmanship/Handwriting
subStrands.description: Using punctuation marks and writing sentences clearly.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge in the use of full stops, commas and question marks appropriately in sentences; and write simple sentences boldly and clearly.

indicators.description: Recognise the use of full stops at the end of a complete sentence, and to separate initials.

exemplars.description: Let learners write sentences on the board and in their books.
Go round and check the sentences written to see if full stops are at the ends.
Discuss the punctuation, full stop, with learners.
Write a passage on the board with all punctuations.
Assist learners to recognise that a full stop is used at the end of a complete sentence, and to separate initials.

indicators.description: Recognise that a comma is used to separate a list of items. It serves as a pause in sentences and speech.

exemplars.description: Write a passage on the board with all the appropriate punctuations.
Discuss the passage with learners, and help them to recognize the punctuation comma.
Assist learners to recognise that a comma is used to separate a list of items. It serves as a pause in sentences and speech.
Let learners write sentences or short passages using the comma.
Write a list of items on the board and ask learners to use the list to form sentences, using the comma to separate the items in the sentence written.

indicators.description: Recognise that a colon is used to list and explain a statement, or to mention a list of items.

exemplars.description: Write a passage on the board with all the appropriate punctuations.
Discuss the use of the colon in the passage.
Assist learners to recognise that a colon is used to list and explain a statement, or to mention a list of items.

indicators.description: Recognise that quotation marks are used when you want to write or quote the same words a person said or wrote.

exemplars.description: Call learners to make some utterances by asking questions.
Write the utterance in quotation marks on the board and discuss with learners.
Write a passage on the board with all punctuations.
Assist learners to recognise that, quotation marks are used when you want to write the same words a person said or wrote.

indicators.description: Write simple sentences.

exemplars.description: Write words on the boards and explain the meaning of those words.
Call learners in turns to form simple sentences with the words.
Write sentences on sentence cards.
Use the sentence cards to help learners write simple and meaningful sentences.

strands.title: Composition Writing
strands.description: Writing narratives, creative stories, descriptive, persuasive, and argumentative essays, as well as letters and academic compositions.

subStrands.title: Narrative Writing
subStrands.description: Using punctuation correctly in narrative writing.

contentStandards.description: Comprehend and use punctuation marks in narrative writing.

indicators.description: Recognise and use commas, full stops, and question marks appropriately in narrative writing.

exemplars.description: Discuss with learners types of writing and explain what narrative writing is.
Give examples of narrative writing to learners to examine.
Discuss with learners the structure and features of narrative writing.
Assist learners to recognise the use of commas, full stops, and question marks appropriately in narrative writing given.
Allow learners to write a narrative of about two hundred words.

indicators.description: Understand and use exclamation mark in narrative writing appropriately.

exemplars.description: Give a long narrative writing piece to learners.
Discuss the content of the narrative writing with learners.
Allow learners to recognise the exclamation marks used in the given piece.
Let learners read the narrative piece in their groups.
Assist learners to understand the use of exclamation marks in narrative writing appropriately.

indicators.description: Know the appropriate use of colon and quotation marks in narrative writing.

exemplars.description: With a given narrative writing piece, allow learners to discuss in groups the punctuations used in the narrative writing.
Assist learners to know the use of the colon and quotation marks in narrative writing appropriately through discussion.

subStrands.title: Creative/ Free Writing
subStrands.description: Writing short and long imaginative and real stories.

contentStandards.description: Show an understanding of creating and writing longer stories on their own.

indicators.description: Write a short story on their own.

exemplars.description: Discuss with learners things that are considered in writing a story.
In groups, ask learners to create a short story and read to the class.
Give a few words on the board as a guide for learners to write a short story.

indicators.description: Write an imaginative longer story on their own.

exemplars.description: Ask a learner to tell a story.
Discuss with learners what an imaginative story is.
In groups, ask learners to write an imaginative story of about three hundred words and present to the class.
Write sentences on flashcards.
Use the sentences on the flashcards to help learners to write an imaginative longer story on their own.

indicators.description: Create a story that relates to their environment.

exemplars.description: Discuss some environmental issues with learners such as flood, bushfire, climate change pollution, etc.
Give learners some guiding sentences on the board.
Put learners in groups and guide them to create a story about a selected issue on the environment for each group.

subStrands.title: Descriptive Writing
subStrands.description: Writing descriptive essays about people, objects, and processes.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge of writing descriptive essays using controlled composition or on their own.

indicators.description: Write simple descriptive essays about human beings using controlled composition.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a short descriptive essay on a cardboard.
Encourage and monitor learners to write simple descriptive essays about human beings using controlled composition.

indicators.description: Give simple descriptive essays about objects using controlled composition.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a simple descriptive essay on a cardboard.
Let learners write simple descriptive essays about objects using controlled composition.

indicators.description: Write their own simple descriptive essays on given topics.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a simple descriptive essay on a cardboard.
Guide learners to write simple descriptive essays on given topics of at least three paragraphs and read some aloud in class.

subStrands.title: Persuasive Writing
subStrands.description: Writing persuasive essays using controlled composition.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge of writing simple persuasive essays using controlled composition on their own

indicators.description: Write a simple persuasive essay through controlled composition.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a simple persuasive essay on a cardboard.
Read the sample persuasive essays on the cardboard and discuss some of its structure and features.
Let learners compose a simple persuasive essay through controlled composition individually and read some aloud to class.

indicators.description: Write simple persuasive essays about domestic issues.

exemplars.description: Discuss domestic issues with learners.
Use controlled composition to write a simple persuasive essay on a cardboard.
Allow learners to write simple persuasive essays about domestic issues.

indicators.description: Write persuasive essays on given topics.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a simple persuasive essay on a cardboard.
Guide learners to write persuasive essays on given topics.

subStrands.title: Argumentative Writing
subStrands.description: Gathering information and writing argumentative essays.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge and understanding of good argumentative essays by gathering information.

indicators.description: Gather information for the writing of good argumentative essays.

exemplars.description: Discuss the structure of argumentative writing with learners.
Use controlled composition to write a simple argumentative essay on a cardboard.
Read the argumentative essay on the board pointing out the structure.
Let learners understand and recognise how to gather information for the writing of good argumentative essays.

indicators.description: Comprehend and discuss how to write for or against a motion in an argumentative essay.

exemplars.description: Give a topic to the class and put the learners into two groups.
Let one group write for the topic and the other against the topic in class.
Let each group read their write up in class.
Discuss the ways of writing for or against a motion in a given motion in an argumentative essay.
Let individual learners write for or against a given motion.

indicators.description: Write a simple argumentative essay on a given topic.

exemplars.description: Use controlled composition to write a simple argumentative essay on a cardboard.
Guide learners to write a simple argumentative essay on a given topic of about four paragraphs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of creating a journal

indicators.description: Write articles for a journal and edit the articles.

exemplars.description: Show learners a copy of an article.
Discuss with learners some types of articles and their structure.
Discuss with learners what a journal is.
Talk to learners about types of journals.
Guide learners to write a simple article in their groups, and discuss in class.
Create a class journal. Let learners write articles for their class journal.
Assist learners to edit the articles for their class journal by bringing out the features and structure of the article in the journal.

indicators.description: Publish and appreciate the articles in the journal.

exemplars.description: Look at the class journal created.
In their groups, let learners write simple articles on topics on disability and equity, and let other learners edit them.
Ask the learners to publish the article in the created class journal and display in the class.
Put learners in groups and allow each group to read an article from the class journal and discuss the article, bringing out for instance, the moral and the theme.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of creating short literary works.

indicators.description: Write short poems.

exemplars.description: Write a simple short poem on a cardboard.
Discuss some features of a poem with learners.
Use flashcards with short poems on them to help learners compose their own short poems.

indicators.description: Create short prose.

exemplars.description: Show learners samples of prose and discuss some features of prose.
Ask learners to write a simple prose to be read in class.
Give an assignment of prose writing as a competition among learners.

indicators.description: Write a short and simple play.

exemplars.description: Allow learners to watch a simple play.
Discuss the play with learners and bring out its features.
Write out some of the features of a play on the board as a guide.
Ask learners to write a simple play of at least three characters, one of the plays may be dramatised in class and be discussed.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge in the writing of semi-formal letters.

indicators.description: Comprehend and discuss the process in writing good semi-formal letters.

exemplars.description: Discuss letter writing and its structure with learners.
Show a sample of a letter to learners to point out the structure and features.
Discuss the features and types of letters.
Explain to learners the structure of semi-formal letters.
Write a sample semi-formal letter on the board.
Discuss the process involved in writing a semi-formal letter.
Assist learners to understand the process in writing good semi-formal letters.

indicators.description: Write semi-formal letters using controlled composition.

exemplars.description: Write a semi-formal letter on the board.
Assist learners to write semi-formal letters using controlled composition.
Ask learners to point out the features and structure of the semi-formal letter written.

indicators.description: Write good semi-formal letters.

exemplars.description: Read a semi-formal letter to learners.
Guide learners to write good semi-formal letters.

strands.title: Writing Conventions/ Usage
strands.description: Applying grammar rules in written language.

contentStandards.description: Show an understanding in the use of capital letters appropriately.

indicators.description: Understand that capital letters begin proper nouns.

exemplars.description: Write a list of words on the board comprising of common nouns and proper nouns.
Ask learners to group the nouns.
Discuss with learners the proper nouns.
Let learners recognise the use of capital letters to begin the proper nouns.
Ask students to write some more proper nouns on the board.
Ask learners to use some of the proper nouns in sentences.

indicators.description: Comprehend the use of capital letters after a colon.

exemplars.description: Write a paragraph on flash cards with all punctuations used.
Ask learners to recognise where capital letters occur in the paragraph.
Discuss the colon and the use of capitals after the colon.
Use flashcards to help learners understand the use of capital letters after a colon.

indicators.description: Understand the use of capital letters after a question mark.

exemplars.description: Allow learners to read a passage.
Discuss with learners the occurrences of the question mark in the passage.
Let learners recognise the words that occur after the question mark.
Discuss the occurrence of the capital letter to begin the word after the question mark.
Write a few sentences on the board and ask learners to write them out correctly, placing in them question marks and capital letters, etc.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge in the use of punctuation marks in passages.

indicators.description: Recognise and use commas, full stops, and question marks appropriately in writing.

exemplars.description: Show a passage to learners and allow the learners to read.
Read the passage aloud to learners.
Let learners recognise the punctuation used in the passage.
Write a paragraph on a flash card without any punctuations.
Guide learners to use commas, full stops, and question marks appropriately in the writing.

indicators.description: Understand and use exclamation mark in writing appropriately.

exemplars.description: Allow learners to read a passage and discuss the punctuations with learners.
Talk about the exclamation mark.
Write a paragraph on a flash card without some punctuations, e.g. the exclamation mark.
Read the paragraph aloud to learners.
Assist learners to use exclamation marks to punctuate the writing appropriately.

indicators.description: Use colon and quotation marks in writing appropriately.

exemplars.description: Revise the lesson on colon with learners and discuss quotation marks with learners.
Give a short passage and ask learners to put in the colon and quotation marks appropriately.

subStrands.title: Integrating Grammar in Written Language (Use of action words)
subStrands.description: Using action words in present and past tense.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge on use of action words appropriately.

indicators.description: Recognise and use simple present tense action words in sentences.

exemplars.description: Ask learners to do some actions in the class like clap, jump, sit, etc.
Write and read aloud some of the action words mentioned by the learners.
Ask learners to form sentences orally with some of the action words.
Write simple present tense sentences on flashcards.
Call learners in turns to read out the sentences on the flashcards.
Call a learner to say or point out the action word in the sentence on a flashcard.
Give simple present tense action words to learners to form sentences and read out aloud, or show to the class by writing on the board.

indicators.description: Use simple past tense action words in sentences.

exemplars.description: Ask learners to recount what they did the day before.
Write some of the action words mentioned by the learners on the board.
Read aloud to learners the written action words.
Talk to learners about the action and explain to them the action has happened already.
Allow learners to give more action words orally and guide them to put the words in past tense.
Ask learners to use the past tense action words to form simple sentences in writing, or orally.

subStrands.title: Integrating Grammar in Written Language (Use of qualifying words)

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge in the use of adjectives and adverbs.

indicators.description: Recognise and use the types of adjectives (dimension, colour, age)

exemplars.description: Show objects to the class and let learners touch the objects.
Ask learners to describe the objects.
Write on the board some of the words used in describing the objects.
Read aloud the words to learners e.g. blue, big, small, round etc.
Allow learners to use some of the qualifying words to form sentences either written or orally.
Write sentences containing adjectives on flashcards.
Use the flashcards with adjectives written on them to help learners recognise the type of adjectives.
Ask learners to mention adjectives and write them on the board.
Allow learners to use some of the adjectives to form sentences.
Ask learners to put the adjectives written on the board into the different types taught to the learners.
Put learners into groups and give each group one type of adjective to form some sentences with them and read aloud to the class.

indicators.description: Use of comparative and superlative words/adjectives forms in sentences.

exemplars.description: Show two objects of the same type to learners.
Ask learners to compare the objects in terms of size, colour, age, etc.
Write out the words that are used in the sentences to compare the objects.
Explain to learners that the comparative is done either with the use of a word, or the adjectival form changes depending on the language in question.
Talk about the superlative and discuss the words used in a sentence to tell that the object that is described is superlative.

subStrands.title: Integrating Grammar in Written Language (Use of postpositions)

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the use of postpositions.

indicators.description: Recognise and use postpositions in complex sentences.

exemplars.description: Revise postpositions with learners.
Let learners give some examples of postpositions.
Write the postpositions on the board and read them aloud.
Allow learners to form some sentences.
Write sentences with postposition words on flashcards. Read aloud the sentences and allow learners to also read.
Guide learners to recognise post positions in complex sentences.
Allow learners to use some of the written postpositions on the board to form complex sentences.
Explain the structure of a complex sentence to learners.
Assist learners to use postpositions in writing complex sentences.

indicators.description: Recognise postpositions in paragraphs

exemplars.description: Give learners a passage to read or read it to them.
Assist learners to recognise post positions in paragraphs.
Present learners with a mixture of words and allow them to select the postpositions.

subStrands.title: Integrating Grammar in Written Language (Use of simple and compound sentences)

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge in the use of conjunctions in forming compound sentences.

indicators.description: Recognise single conjunctions such as 'but' and 'because' in compound sentences.

exemplars.description: Ask learners to give simple sentences orally and write the sentences on the board.
Discuss how some of the sentences can be put together as one sentence.
Explain to the learners the use of conjunctions as words used to link the sentences.
Give a sample compound sentence and guide learners to recognise the conjunction in it.
Write out other conjunctions and read aloud to learners.
Use flashcards with single conjunctions written on them to assist learners to recognise single conjunctions such as 'but', 'because' in compound sentences.

indicators.description: Use single conjunctions in forming compound sentences.

exemplars.description: Write a mixture of words on the board and lead learners to select the conjunctions.
Ask learners to use the conjunctions to form compound sentences orally or written.
Put learners in a group to write compound sentences and underline the conjunction.

indicators.description: Form compound sentences with appropriate conjunctions.

exemplars.description: Give learners simple sentences and ask them to form compound sentences with them using the appropriate conjunction.
Use flashcards with conjunctions written on them to assist learners to form compound sentences with appropriate conjunctions.
Allow learners to write some conjunctions on the board.

contentStandards.description: Recognise and spell out words correctly.

indicators.description: Write eight and nine-letter words correctly.

exemplars.description: Ask learners to mention words they know and write them on the board.
Group the words according to the number of letters.
Read the letters aloud and guide learners to spell out the words correctly.
Use flashcards with eight and nine letter words written on them to help learners to write eight and nine letter words correctly.

indicators.description: Rearrange letters to form new words.

exemplars.description: Give learners some letters and ask them to form words from those letters.
Say and write on the board eight, and nine letters and help learners rearrange the letters to form new words.

indicators.description: Fill in missing words from passages.

exemplars.description: Write words with some missing sounds. Let learners recognise them and fill in the missing letters.
Using flashcards with sentences that have missing words written on them help learners fill in missing words from passages.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge on the use of conjunctions in writing sentences

indicators.description: Identify conjunctions (because, since, so, although etc.) appropriately in sentences to give reasons, link contrasting ideas and show results

exemplars.description: Revise the lesson on simple conjunctions.
Provide simple sentences and let learners join them using and, or/nor, but.
Introduce because, since, so, although in context.
Guide learners to discover the functions of these conjunctions.
Have them practise using these conjunctions in their own sentences.
Provide a passage and have learners identify the conjunctions in the passage.
Let learners form pairs of simple sentences and join them with the conjunctions identified.

subStrands.title: Building the Love and Culture of Reading in Learners

contentStandards.description: Exhibit the ability to read other materials like newspapers, novels, other than the class Reader alone.

indicators.description: Read aloud passages from novels and newspapers with correct pronunciation and tone.

exemplars.description: Read a passage aloud to learners.
Use flashcards with three to four word sentences written on them to assist learners with correct pronunciation and intonation.
Let learners bring other materials on literary works like magazines or newspapers to read.
Call learners to read paragraph by paragraph to check the correct pronunciation.

indicators.description: Demonstrate correct speech, rhythm and tone.

exemplars.description: Read a newspaper or novel aloud to learners with the correct tone and rhythm.
Allow learners to demonstrate correct speech, rhythm and tone.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge in reading sentences, paragraphs and stories aloud.

indicators.description: Read aloud passages with correct pronunciation and tone.

exemplars.description: Read a passage of about seven paragraphs aloud to learners.
Lead learners to read aloud passages with correct pronunciation and intonation.

indicators.description: Demonstrate correct speech, rhythm and tone.

exemplars.description: Demonstrate correct speech, rhythm and tone.
Lead learners to demonstrate correct speech, rhythm and tone.

subStrands.title: Reading Texts, Poems, Narrative, and Short Stories and Respond to them

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge in reading materials other than the reader provided in class with understanding.

indicators.description: Read short texts, narratives or stories from other materials with correct intonation/tone.

exemplars.description: Read a text aloud to the hearing of learners.
Guide learners to read short texts, narratives or stories from other materials with correct intonation.
Let learners read paragraph each of the text to the class.

indicators.description: Answer questions on the narratives/passage read.

exemplars.description: Learners read a passage to the hearing of others learners.
Lead learners to answer questions on the passage read orally then write them into their books.

indicators.description: Retell the short stories or narratives read.

exemplars.description: Read a passage to the hearing of learners.
Guide learners to re-tell the short stories or narratives read.

indicators.description: Read paragraphs, passages and stories of different texts.

exemplars.description: Read a paragraph to the hearing of learners.
Give learners the opportunity to read paragraphs, passages and stories of different texts to the class.

indicators.description: Answer factual questions based on the passage read.

exemplars.description: Read a passage to the hearing of learners.
Help learners to read a text.
Let them answer factual questions based on the passage read.
Ask learners to narrate what they read.

indicators.description: Write a summary of passage/text read.

exemplars.description: Read a passage to the hearing of learners.
Lead learners to read a text.
Guide them to summarize the passage read.
